newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges ex-Tyson chairman, friend.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges ex-Tyson chairman, friend.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday it filed insider trading charges against Donald John Tyson, former chairman of Tyson Foods Inc, and a friend in connection with Tyson Foods' acquisition of Arctic Alaska Fisheries Corp in 1992.

In a civil complaint filed in a federal district court in Arkansas, the SEC alleged that Tyson's friend, Frederick Lee Cameron, bought Arctic Alaska shares based on a tip he received from the then chairman of the food company.
According to the SEC complaint, Cameron bought 9,000 shares of Arctic Alaska at $6.625 a share or $59,625 on June 2, 1992 after receiving word from Tyson about the pending acquisition.
Cameron sold the shares on June 16, the day the deal was announced at $11.75 a share, for $105,750, making a profit of $46,125, the SEC alleged.
Simultaneously with the filing of the complaint, Tyson and Cameron agreed to settle the charges, without admitting or denying the SEC's allegations, the agency said.
Pending final court approval, the defendants consented to be permanently enjoined from violating anti-fraud provisions of federal securities laws, the SEC said.
Cameron also agreed to forfeit $46,125 -- the alleged illegal profits -- and pay interest totalling $18,153. Both Cameron and Tyson also agreed to each pay a civil penalty of $46,125, the SEC said.
